knowledge:
- key_parameters: K=The number of cell types ;; confuse_rate=The proportion of cells from one cell type being assigned to other cell types in create_simMat ;; similarity_mat=A matrix indicating the misclassification rate between different cell types ;; base_model=Set to 'FULL' to compare the full model and a model without the tested factor (controlling for other factors) ;; fix_phi=A global over-dispersion parameter estimated using getPhi to apply to all cell types and avoid overfitting ;; reference=A vector of cell types to use as reference/normalization terms
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when comparing cell type proportions/compositions across multiple samples/conditions or continuous covariates in scRNA-seq data, especially when there are small numbers of replicates and high uncertainty in cell clustering.
- pitfalls: Low number of replicates can cause a warning "Possible convergence problem. Optimization process code: 10 (see ?optim)", which does not affect final results. Fitting phi (over-dispersion) for each cell type individually might lead to over-fitting; use getPhi and fix_phi to apply a global phi instead. Using only one cell type as a reference is not recommended; it is recommended to use more than one cell type and more than 20% of total cells as the reference group. Automatic reference cell selection via detect_reference is challenging and should be performed with caution.

workflows.name: differential_composition_analysis
workflows.intent: Detect differential cell type composition abundances between conditions in scRNA-seq data while correcting for cell misclassification.
input: sim_count (matrix of cell counts per sample and cell type)
knnGraphs (Seurat KNN graph for similarity estimation)
svmDF (data frame of features and labels for SVM estimation)
workflows.stages: 1. Estimate the similarity/confusion matrix using one of three methods (create_simMat, knn_simMat, or svm_simMat) ;; 2. (Optional) Estimate a global over-dispersion parameter phi using getPhi to prevent overfitting ;; 3. (Optional) Detect or define reference cell types for normalization using detect_reference ;; 4. Perform differential abundance analysis using dcats_GLM with the count matrix, design matrix, similarity matrix, and optional reference or dispersion parameters.
workflows.code:
simil_mat = create_simMat(K = 3, confuse_rate = 0.2)

knn_mat = knn_simMat(simulation$knnGraphs, simulation$labels)

svm_mat = svm_simMat(Kang2017$svmDF)

dcats_GLM(sim_count, sim_design, similarity_mat = simil_mat)

dcats_GLM(sim_count, sim_design, similarity_mat = simil_mat, base_model='FULL')

phi = DCATS::getPhi(sim_count, sim_design)
dcats_GLM(sim_count, sim_design, similarity_mat = simil_mat, fix_phi = phi)

dcats_GLM(sim_count, sim_design, similarity_mat = simil_mat, reference = c("A", "B"))

reference_cell = detect_reference(sim_count, sim_design, similarity_mat = simil_mat)
dcats_GLM(sim_count, sim_design, similarity_mat = simil_mat, reference = reference_cell$ordered_celltype[1:2])
